findings.claim: Z5 defines the differential contract as 'a transpile diff is WARN unless ruchy run stdout also differs'. This completely ignores runtime semantic regressions if the transpiled code remains textually identical.
findings.fix: Rewrite Z5 stage 4 rules: 'a transpile diff is WARN; a ruchy run stdout diff is FAIL (regardless of transpile text)'. Add a DoD mutation that modifies interpreter output without changing transpile output to prove the gate turns red.

findings.claim: Z3 aliases `trueno` to `aprender-compute`, leaving transpiled `trueno::` paths identical but changing the interpreter runtime from 0.27 to 0.65. Combined with Z5's logic flaw, this semantic drift is completely undetected.
findings.fix: Fix Z5, and add an explicit test script in `examples/` using `trueno::Vector` and `aprender::preprocessing::PCA` to guarantee differential coverage of the version upgrade.

findings.claim: Z4 runs `ruchy migrate-4to5` on `examples/`. The Z5 differential compares 4.2.1 and HEAD on this migrated file, masking any runtime output changes (e.g. stringified variables, shadowing) caused by the migration itself since both binaries run the identical migrated code.
findings.fix: Z4's differential coverage must compare 4.2.1 running the unmigrated file (from git checkout 4.2.1) against HEAD running the migrated file.

findings.claim: Z8 ports polars dataframes. Since no dataframe examples appear in the `transpile-diff-examples.txt` evidence despite the API change, the differential test will silently miss any regressions in the ported dataframe output.
findings.fix: Add a dataframe script to `examples/` to ensure the differential test actually exercises the polars 0.55 port.

findings.claim: Z6 adds `debug_assert!` macros to hot paths. These do not change release output, and any panics on valid input are caught by the `dispatch_contracts` property test which runs in debug mode.
